chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ayesha: 'O Ayesha! The obscenity, had it been represented by an image, would be an evil image'.

key_terms.الْفُحْش: Obscenity, foulness, or ugliness in speech and conduct
key_terms.مُمَثَّلًا: Represented, depicted, or given a form/image
key_terms.مِثَالُ سَوْءٍ: An evil image or example of ugliness

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he says obscenity would be an 'evil image' if it had one?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s address to Aisha, emphasizing that obscenity (al-fush) possesses an intrinsic moral ugliness so profound that its mere conceptualization would be repulsive. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that foul speech is not merely a social breach but a fundamental defect in character, reflecting the inner state of the soul.
